name: Acts of the Apostles
kicker: New Testament history of the early Church · Pentecost and Paul’s journeys
dates: Usually dated to the late 1st century CE
briefing: In the Acts of the Apostles, the fifth book of the New Testament, a rushing wind fills a room in Jerusalem and tongues of fire rest on Jesus’s followers, who begin speaking in languages they never learned. That scene, called Pentecost, launches the book’s story of the early Church spreading from Jerusalem toward Rome. Its second half follows Paul through riots, prison, and a shipwreck on Malta.
answerHtml: Acts of the Apostles (or Book of Acts; prompt on Luke-Acts)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Parts of this book switch from telling what “they” did to what “we” did, suggesting to many readers that its author traveled with its main missionary. Like an earlier book by the same author, this book is addressed to a man named Theophilus [“thee-OFF-ih-lus”].
tossups.r: Tradition says both books were written by Luke. For 10 points, name this fifth book of the New Testament.

tossups.p: In this book, a young man named Eutychus [“YOO-tih-kus”] falls asleep during a long sermon and drops from a third-story window, but the preacher brings him back to life. Later in this book, that preacher survives a shipwreck on Malta and shakes off a snake that bites his hand.
tossups.r: That preacher, Paul, ends this book under house arrest in Rome. For 10 points, name this New Testament book that comes right after the Gospels.

tossups.p: In this book, the church in Antioch sends Barnabas and Saul on a mission to the island of Cyprus. This book also says that the followers of Jesus were first called “Christians” in Antioch.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this book of the Bible that describes the Holy Spirit coming down at Pentecost.

tossups.p: The word “simony” [“SY-muh-nee”], for buying or selling church offices, comes from a magician in this book who offers the apostles money for the power to give people the Holy Spirit. Earlier in this book, a couple named Ananias and Sapphira die suddenly after lying to Peter about money from selling their land.
tossups.r: This book begins with Jesus rising into heaven. For 10 points, name this New Testament book about the early Church.

tossups.p: In this book, a speaker in Athens points to an altar inscribed “To an unknown god” in a speech at the Areopagus [“air-ee-OP-uh-gus”], or Mars Hill. In that speech, he says that in God “we live and move and have our being.”
tossups.r: That speaker, Paul, makes several missionary journeys in this book. For 10 points, name this fifth book of the New Testament.

tossups.p: In this book, a seller of purple cloth named Lydia, often called the first recorded convert in Europe, is baptized at Philippi. Later in Philippi, an earthquake shakes open the doors of a prison where two missionaries have been singing hymns at midnight, and their jailer is baptized.
tossups.r: Those missionaries were Paul and Silas. For 10 points, name this New Testament book that ends with Paul in Rome.

tossups.p: In this book, the evangelist Philip meets a court official of the queen of Ethiopia who is reading the prophet Isaiah while riding in his chariot. Philip explains the passage to him, and the official is baptized in water beside the road.
tossups.r: This book also describes Saul’s conversion on the road to Damascus. For 10 points, name this book that follows the Gospel of John.

tossups.p: In this book, Peter has a vision of a great sheet full of animals that the Law of Moses called unclean, and a voice tells him not to call anything unclean that God has made clean. He then has a Roman centurion named Cornelius [“kor-NEEL-yus”] and his household baptized.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this New Testament book whose second chapter describes the coming of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost.

tossups.p: In the fifteenth chapter of this book, a council in Jerusalem decides, on the advice of James, that non-Jewish believers do not have to follow the whole Law of Moses, after Peter, Barnabas, and Paul describe their work among the Gentiles.
tossups.r: This book also tells of Stephen, the first Christian martyr. For 10 points, name this book written by the author of the Gospel of Luke.

tossups.p: In this book, the respected teacher Gamaliel [“guh-MAY-lee-ul”] advises the council called the Sanhedrin [“san-HEE-drin”] to leave the apostles alone, saying that if their movement comes from God, no one will be able to stop it. Paul later says that he studied under Gamaliel.
tossups.r: This book also describes how the Holy Spirit came at Pentecost. For 10 points, name this book that tells the history of the early Church.

tossups.p: Near the start of this book, Peter stands up among about 120 believers, and they cast lots to choose Matthias [“muh-THY-us”] over Joseph Barsabbas [“bar-SAB-us”] to replace Judas Iscariot as one of the Twelve.
tossups.r: This book later follows Paul’s missionary journeys. For 10 points, name this New Testament book written by the author of Luke’s Gospel.

tossups.p: In this book, an angel leads Peter out of prison, and when he knocks at the gate of a house where believers are praying, a servant girl named Rhoda is so overjoyed that she runs inside to tell them without opening the gate.
tossups.r: This book also describes Pentecost and the conversion of Saul. For 10 points, name this New Testament book.

tossups.p: In this book, a silversmith named Demetrius, who made small silver shrines of the goddess Artemis, stirs up a riot in Ephesus, and the crowd shouts “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!” for about two hours.
tossups.r: The missionary whose preaching angered Demetrius was Paul. For 10 points, name this fifth book of the New Testament.

tossups.p: After a man who had never walked is healed at Lystra [“LISS-truh”] in this book, the crowd hails Barnabas as Zeus and his companion as Hermes, and the two missionaries tear their clothes to stop the people from offering sacrifices to them.
tossups.r: That companion was Paul, who had been blinded by a light on the road to Damascus. For 10 points, name this book.

tossups.p: In this book, one of seven men chosen to hand out food to widows gives a long speech retelling Israel’s history from Abraham to Solomon. The witnesses at that man’s death laid their cloaks at the feet of a young man named Saul.
tossups.r: That man, Stephen, became the first Christian martyr when a crowd stoned him. For 10 points, name this New Testament book.

clues.t: Fifth book of the New Testament, right after the four Gospels; it tells the history of the early Church
Written by the author of the Gospel of Luke, traditionally Luke the physician
Chapter 2: at Pentecost, the Holy Spirit comes as tongues of fire, and the apostles speak in other languages
Follows Paul’s missionary journeys and ends with him under house arrest in Rome
Saul is blinded by a light on the road to Damascus and becomes a follower of Jesus
Like Luke’s Gospel, it is addressed to a man named Theophilus
Begins with Jesus’s ascension into heaven, forty days after his resurrection
Stephen, one of seven chosen helpers, becomes the first Christian martyr when a crowd stones him
Matthias is chosen by casting lots to replace Judas Iscariot as one of the Twelve
Believers are first called “Christians” at Antioch, whose church sends Barnabas and Saul on a mission to Cyprus
The Council of Jerusalem (chapter 15) rules that non-Jewish believers need not follow the whole Law of Moses
Peter’s vision of a sheet of unclean animals; then the Roman centurion Cornelius is baptized
Ananias and Sapphira die suddenly after lying to Peter about money from a land sale
Its first half centers on Peter, and its second half centers on Paul
The “we” passages, told in the first person plural, suggest that the author traveled with Paul
Simon Magus tries to buy the power to give the Holy Spirit, which gives us the word “simony”
Philip baptizes an Ethiopian court official who was reading Isaiah in his chariot
Paul preaches at the Areopagus (Mars Hill) in Athens about an altar “to an unknown god”
In Philippi, Lydia, a seller of purple cloth, is baptized; an earthquake opens the prison of Paul and Silas, and their jailer is baptized
Eutychus falls asleep during Paul’s long sermon, drops from a third-story window, and is brought back to life
Paul is shipwrecked on Malta and shakes off a viper without harm
An angel frees Peter from prison; the servant girl Rhoda is so excited she forgets to open the gate
Gamaliel, Paul’s teacher, tells the Sanhedrin that if the apostles’ movement is from God, it cannot be stopped
Demetrius the silversmith starts a riot in Ephesus: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
At Lystra, crowds hail Barnabas as Zeus and Paul as Hermes
Stephen’s long speech retells Israel’s history from Abraham to Solomon; witnesses laid their cloaks at Saul’s feet

trap.title: The book, not its heroes
trap.body: Most clues follow Peter or Paul, so early buzzers name a person instead of the book. Others hear “by the author of Luke” or “addressed to Theophilus” and answer the Gospel of Luke, the first half of the same two-part work. Paul’s own letters, such as Romans and Galatians, are separate books.
trap.fix: If the question says “this book,” answer “Acts” (or “Acts of the Apostles”). Theophilus plus Jesus’s birth or parables means the Gospel of Luke; Theophilus plus Pentecost, Stephen, or Paul’s journeys means Acts.
trap.line: Real answer line: Acts of the Apostles (or Book of Acts; prompt on Luke-Acts)
